To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) Ca2+-activated channels are lost in vesiculation procedures, (b) they can be preserved in a single-step vesiculation procedure, and (c) they are activated in an all or none fashion by Ca2+.
(1) the Ca2+- activated K+ channel is a major component of the ionic conductance of the human red cell membrane and (2) it has a high affinity for ionized calcium.
the calcium-activated K+ channel is present in human red cell membranes and that the calcium response can be lost during vesiculation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of the Ca2+ activated K+ channel of the human red cell membrane.
the properties of a calcium- activated potassium channel in a membrane preparation which has the advantages of simplicity, stability and ease of handling.
the properties of the Ca2+ activated K+ channel in human red cell IOVs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca2+-sensitive K+ channel is present in one-step IOVs and that the channel is a functional entity.
the Ca2+-sensitive potassium channel in human red cell membranes is a single protein with a high calcium sensitivity and a high potassium permeability.
the Ca2+-dependent K+ channel is a major component of the human red cell plasma membrane and is preserved in one-step IOVs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ca2+-dependent K+ channel in red cell membranes has a very low turnover number, but is very efficient in its response to calcium activation, and is not subject to the control mechanisms which operate on other membrane transport systems.
the Ca2+-dependent component of 86Rb+ efflux from one- step IOVs is a property of the Ca2+ activated K+ channel.
Ca2+-activated channels are preserved and functional in one-step IOVs from human red cells and that they can be studied under controlled conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ca2+-dependent K+ channel can be studied in a single-step inside-out vesicle preparation from human red cell membrane, which preserves the Ca2+-dependence of K+ transport, but not in vesicles prepared from the same membrane using the two-step method of Steck and his co-workers.

the Ca2+- activated K+ channel in human red cell membrane vesicles is a single protein, with a high affinity for ionized calcium, that can be studied in a reconstituted form in a single step inside-out vesicles.
it is possible to preserve the calcium-activated K+ channel during vesiculation, provided the vesiculation conditions are carefully controlled.
